subject: Next steps: Redwood vs hyperscalers — observability & ops tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Joe Reynolds <joe.reynolds@acme-observability.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Redwood vs hyperscalers — observability & ops tests

Hi Joe / Tina —

Thanks again for a great discussion today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Recap (call highlights):
- Primary goal: validate inference economics and operational observability for your production use (batch ML-driven alert enrichment and real-time triage).
- Key concerns: per-token latency and cost at 95th percentile, tracing and attribution (request -> token billing), and auditability for incident investigation.
- Hyperscaler comparison: you want apples-to-apples throughput/latency and an ops picture — not just endpoint latency but end-to-end tracing and token-level cost breakdowns.

Proposed next steps:
1) Bench plan: Redwood will run the following tests vs two hyperscaler endpoints you nominate (e.g., AWS Bedrock + Azure OpenAI):
   - 1k request burst with mixed lengths (16/128/512 tokens) to capture tail latency
   - Sustained 5-min throughput test to measure throughput and token cost
   - Tracing capture: sample traces for 100 requests (we’ll provide a Datadog/OpenTelemetry exporter)
2) Observability checks: we’ll provide a sample trace config and an example dashboard JSON you can import to compare metrics (latency percentiles, tokens/tokenized, KV cache hit rate, per-route cost).
3) Mutual action plan (attached draft): timelines, responsibilities, success criteria, and required access (test credentials, preferred hyperscaler endpoints).
4) Security/compliance ask: we’ll attach SOC2 summary and a short checklist of evidence you requested during the call.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-comparison.xlsx (matrix), mutual-action-plan-draft.pdf, sample-trace-config.yml

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm the two hyperscaler endpoints you want us to include?
- Do you prefer Datadog or an OpenTelemetry sink for traces?
- Any specific traffic profile we should simulate beyond the mixed-lengths above?

I’ll coordinate scheduling for the execution window next week once you confirm endpoints. Laura and Dev are looped for technical coordination — Dev will own the test run.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Joe Reynolds <joe.reynolds@acme-observability.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tina Park <tina.park@acme-observability.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: Redwood vs hyperscalers — observability & ops tests

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap and the clear plan. A few quick items:
- Please include AWS Bedrock and Azure OpenAI for the hyperscaler runs.
- We use Datadog (APM + dashboards) — Datadog traces would be ideal.
- For traffic profile: focus 70% short prompts (~16 tokens), 20% medium (128), 10% long (512). Also include a 30s spike run to simulate incident traffic.

Two asks from my side:
1) Can you provide a short table of expected token cost per platform for the baseline model you’ll test? Even rough numbers will help our initial procurement checks.
2) We’ll need a one-page list of required network/credential access so we can get SRE to provision test accounts.

If that works, I’ll block 2 hours next Tuesday for the sync/test kickoff and loop in SRE.

Thanks — Joe

Subject: Re: Next steps: Redwood vs hyperscalers — observability & ops tests

Thanks Joe — this is perfect. Notes inline and next deliverables: 

Inline:
- Endpoints confirmed: AWS Bedrock + Azure OpenAI.
- Datadog as tracing sink — will use our OTLP exporter to post spans.
- Traffic mix updated (70/20/10) + 30s spike.

Deliverables we’ll send by Monday EOD:
1) Cost estimates (ballpark per-token cost for the model variant we’ll test) across Redwood, Bedrock, Azure. These are run-rate estimates for the test profile only (not final procurement).
2) Test run spec (detailed steps, sample payloads, time windows).
3) Network/credentials checklist for SRE.
4) Updated MAP (I attached a draft with timelines).

Technical notes / differentiation to highlight in the evaluation:
- Observability: Redwood provides token-level cost attribution and per-request trace linking to tokens generated, which is different from many hyperscaler endpoints that only expose endpoint-level metrics. We’ll show an example dashboard mapping traces to token billing for a request.
- Operational tooling: Continuous KV cache warmup and prefix caching reduces burst costs for your profile — we’ll run one test with and without caching enabled to show delta.
- Graceful fallbacks: if a model variant returns degraded output under load, our routing can automatically fall back to a compatible variant with reduced latency — we can simulate this in the spike test.

Attachments included: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-comparison.xlsx, mutual-action-plan-draft.pdf, sample-trace-config.yml

Proposed kickoff: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:00-12:00 PT (please confirm). I’ll include Dev and Markus for the run.

Marissa
